title: Graph Atlas: Four Views of a Computing System
problem:
How do four different, evidence-grounded diagram layouts explain distinct properties of one hypothetical campus research-job gateway? The study is a Computer Science publishing and diagram-readability exercise, not an evaluation of a deployed service. Its source of truth is the one saved constructed-design session, which contains four explicit diagram specifications. Compare exactly four views in a short paper, placing one diagram beside the explanation it supports: (1) a hierarchical decision flow, (2) a block architecture with trust boundaries, (3) a cyclic network describing qualitative congestion-control feedback, and (4) a sequential timeline of one authorized job. Preserve all nodes, directed edges, labels, and boundaries; set each diagram's layout to the corresponding explicit type instead of guessing. Use plain English for technical reasoning and avoid ornamental equations. Distinguish constructed behavior and hypothetical external connections from measurements. Do not claim that any observed throughput, availability, latency, or measured causal impact exists. No external source is required to describe this design fixture.

The four specified views follow. They are the research subject and desired visual content, not suggestions to invent or modify:

1. ADMISSION DECISION FLOW (hierarchical). A request follows policy checks, with rejection and accepted dispatch as distinct branches. This is a dependency and decision view, not a timeline. Nodes: ingress=Receive research job; policy=Check identity and data policy; denied=Reject disallowed request; admitted=Admit authorized request; queue=Enqueue authorized job. Directed edges: ingress -> policy [request evaluated]; policy -> denied [disallowed]; policy -> admitted [allowed]; admitted -> queue [schedule admitted job].

2. SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE AND TRUST BOUNDARIES (architecture). The origin campus controls authentication, policy and local execution; an external provider is hypothetical and requires separate authorization. Nodes: client=Campus research client; identity=Campus identity authority; policy=Policy enforcement gateway; scheduler=Job scheduler; local=Campus GPU worker; external=Optional approved external provider. Directed edges: client -> identity [authenticate user]; identity -> policy [assert campus identity]; policy -> scheduler [approved job only]; scheduler -> local [local dispatch]; scheduler -> external [only with separate approval]. Boundaries: Origin-campus authority boundary contains client, identity, policy, scheduler, local; External provider domain (hypothetical) contains external.

3. CONGESTION FEEDBACK LOOP (network). Input load, queue depth, latency, and admission throttling form a cycle; feedback direction is part of the designed controller, not empirical causality. Nodes: arrival=Admitted arrival load; backlog=Queue backlog; delay=Observed queue delay; throttle=Admission throttle. Directed edges: arrival -> backlog [increases backlog]; backlog -> delay [increases delay]; delay -> throttle [triggers throttling]; throttle -> arrival [reduces admitted load].

4. ORDERED EXECUTION TRACE (timeline). The planned trace consists of five ordered phases; this is event order, with no fabricated timestamps, durations, or performance measurements. Nodes: submit=Job submitted; authorize=Policy authorization recorded; enqueue=Job queued; execute=Worker executes job; audit=Result and audit record committed. Directed edges: submit -> authorize [precedes]; authorize -> enqueue [precedes]; enqueue -> execute [precedes]; execute -> audit [precedes].

Research outcome expected: explain why different diagram types expose distinct aspects of the same proposed system, which assumptions each reveals, and why an evidence-based renderer must not invent missing data. The paper should demonstrate all four figures if diagrams are enabled, while retaining the evidence-bound, skeptical status of this constructed fixture.

strategies.title: Compare four complementary gateway diagrams
strategies.approach: Study four representations of the same hypothetical research-job gateway. Treat each saved, explicit diagram_spec as the primary constructed-design evidence. Compare (A) authorized decision flow, (B) system architecture and domain boundaries, (C) qualitative feedback cycle, and (D) ordered execution trace. Evaluate whether each view preserves its exact directed edges, edge labels, and node membership. Note that none of the representations constitutes a measured performance result or independently validated production system. The short paper should use four clearly captioned figures, one per view, with plain-English explanation.
